subject: bigmouth buffalo fish
title: This Plain Lake Fish Was Thought to Live 20 Years. One Hit 112

scenes.text: Scientists thought this lake fish lived twenty years. They were off by nearly a century.
It's the bigmouth buffalo, a big plain fish from Minnesota lakes.
Then researchers counted the rings in its ear stones. One fish was one hundred twelve years old.
Of nearly four hundred fish aged, five were over one hundred, and many were in their eighties.
How did they prove it? Carbon from nineteen-fifties nuclear tests left a time stamp inside the stones.
And the oldest fish show no sign of aging. Their immune systems are as strong as the young ones'.

description:
The bigmouth buffalo, once thought to live about 20 years, was shown in 2019 to reach 112, the oldest age-validated freshwater bony fish known.
Researchers confirmed the ages with bomb radiocarbon in the fish's ear stones; of nearly 400 aged, five were over 100, and a later study found no decline in immunity or telomeres with age.
What animal do you think lives longest in your local lake?
first_comment: In some lakes almost no young buffalo have hatched since the 1930s, so the whole population is grandparents. What other animal do you think is secretly ancient?
